title: There's nothing better than both parties win
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Have you ever settled a fight so that both sides could walk away with something?

groups.heading: There's nothing better than both parties win

lines.text: As Jose retells it, the other side wanted twenty-five million dollars and would go away. Jose said: think of the stress. He is still losing money, and now he needs to cough up another twenty-five million.

They settled on the twenty-five million, he said, and we know the author knows how to negotiate terms. You learn an incredible amount of wisdom from negotiating terms. Maybe you don't have all the money, but you can negotiate terms so that both parties win.

One thing I really like about him is that he is always fair, Jose said. He doesn't have the attitude of: I won the negotiation, they lost. He defends himself if he is attacked, but he is always fair and just. There is nothing better than both parties win.
Jose read a line from the author after the settlement.
But this was my biggest win so far.
What a great statement, Jose said. He is very conscious of all the things he is achieving, and he is very happy with his achievements.
A student said one thing they took away was that the author is very aware of cost, even in his personal life. Jose agreed.
What could you settle on terms where both sides win?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a negotiation or dispute you are in or expect.
Write what you want, and what the other side wants.
Write terms you could offer so both sides win.
Write how you will stay fair, even while you defend yourself.
Write what you will celebrate when it is settled.

check.q: What did Jose say you can negotiate if you don't have all the money?
What did Jose say about the author in a negotiation?
What did Jose say is better than anything else in a deal?

recap: Negotiate terms so both parties win, and stay fair.
